html:
Manmohan Singh was the finance minister who opened India's economy in 1991 and later prime minister for ten years, from 2004 to 2014. He was the first Sikh to hold that office.

He was born in 1932 in a village of western Punjab without a school or electricity. His family fled to India at Partition. He won scholarships to Cambridge and Oxford and spent thirty years as a government economist, rising to head the Reserve Bank.

In June 1991 India had foreign money for two weeks of imports, and its gold had been flown abroad as security for a loan. The new prime minister, P. V. Narasimha Rao, made Singh finance minister. In a few weeks he devalued the rupee, cut import duties and ended most industrial licences (see economic liberalisation). He told Parliament, quoting Victor Hugo, that no power on earth can stop an idea whose time has come.

In 2004 Congress won, and its leader Sonia Gandhi chose him as prime minister. Growth reached 8 to 9 per cent. His government passed a law guaranteeing rural work, a right to information law, and a nuclear agreement with the United States. Corruption scandals marked his second term.

He was quiet and personally honest. He died in December 2024.
